patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient16; S1S3 identifies this case. Maternally inherited hemizygous c115_116del V39Ffs*14; early motor/language delay, IQ74, autism, macroglossia and hydronephrosis/pelviureteral obstruction requiring surgery. S1 cardiac study normal: packet PDA contradicted. Individual facial row differs substantially from packet; no proof of multilocus diagnosis.

evidence.locator: Supplementary case report Patient16, PDF pages20–21

genotype.statement: Coding and protein allele match Table2/S1; male hemizygosity matches source. VCF representation matches Table2; differently normalized HGVS genomic indel positions in packet have not been independently sequence-normalized.
limitations: No independent genomic reference/normalization check; all allele representations retained.

segregation.statement: Maternal per individualS1 row6; Trio testing described in row7.

phase.statement: Single ZFX allele; cis/trans phase is not a biallelic disease requirement. Maternal/de novo source segregation as separately assessed.

evidence.locator: Supplementary case report Patient16, PDF pages20–21

limitations: No additional haplotype or mosaic fraction measurements supplied.

causal_confidence.statement: Maternally inherited hemizygous c115_116del V39Ffs*14; early motor/language delay, IQ74, autism, macroglossia and hydronephrosis/pelviureteral obstruction requiring surgery. S1 cardiac study normal: packet PDA contradicted. Individual facial row differs substantially from packet; no proof of multilocus diagnosis. Allvariants originally laboratoryVUS because ZFX was a candidate gene; authors putatively upgrade using study evidence and acknowledge ACMG novel-gene limitations. Functional evidence supports gene/variant mechanisms, not automatic clinical pathogenicity of every individual.

causal_confidence.statement: De novo heterozygous T771M; IQ120 and normal development, ASD/ADHD/anxiety, macroglossia and hypercalcemia with inappropriately normal PTH. patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient6A; S1G3 identifies this case. Maternally inherited hemizygous Y774C, pedigreeIII:3; IQ60, hypotonia, macroglossia, seizures, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism/osteoporosis, high myopia/retinal detachment. Hyperparathyroidism is NORMAL in S1 and narrative, despite affected carrier women. PHF6 intron3 microdeletion judged nonclinical by authors.

genotype.statement: Coding and protein allele match Table2/S1; male hemizygosity matches source. patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient6B; S1H3 identifies this case. Maternally inherited hemizygous Y774C, pedigreeIII:10; IQ67, DD, macroglossia, scoliosis, glaucoma/SNHL, PDA/PFO with neonatal pulmonary hypertension. Parathyroid normal. Earlier delayed puberty subsequently progressed normally; pulmonary hypertension must not silently become systemic hypertension.

This is an unresolved source annotation discrepancy, not a resolved liftover.

causal_confidence.statement: Maternally inherited hemizygous Y774C, pedigreeIII:10; IQ67, DD, macroglossia, scoliosis, glaucoma/SNHL, PDA/PFO with neonatal pulmonary hypertension. Parathyroid normal. Earlier delayed puberty subsequently progressed normally; pulmonary hypertension must not silently become systemic hypertension. Functional evidence supports gene/variant mechanisms, not automatic clinical pathogenicity of every individual.

patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient6C; S1I3 identifies this case. Maternally inherited heterozygous Y774C, pedigreeIII:11 A/G, manifesting female with skewed X-inactivation; mild speech/learning difficulties, macroglossia, neonatal OSA, dysmorphism. S1 says no motor delay, walking18months; LD does not establish ID. Parathyroid normal; hyperthyroidism reported. Hemizygous packet contradicted.

Table2/S1 use NM_003410.4:c2321A>G,NC_000023.11:g24211279A>G; Figure3 caption instead prints g24229396A>G and c2438A>G while retaining Tyr774Cys. causal_confidence.statement: Maternally inherited heterozygous Y774C, pedigreeIII:11 A/G, manifesting female with skewed X-inactivation; mild speech/learning difficulties, macroglossia, neonatal OSA, dysmorphism. patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient7; S1J3 identifies this case. De novo hemizygous Y774C; DD/mildID, hypotonia, macroglossia/cleft palate, hernias, brain hemorrhages, airway malacia/stenosis. Main article attributes aortic root dilation/beta blocker to patient7, but individual S1 and case report say normal echocardiogram: source conflict retained.

genotype.statement: Coding and protein allele match Table2/S1; male hemizygosity matches source. Table2/S1 use NM_003410.4:c2321A>G,NC_000023.11:g24211279A>G; Figure3 caption instead prints g24229396A>G and c2438A>G while retaining Tyr774Cys. This is an unresolved source annotation discrepancy, not a resolved liftover.
limitations: No independent genomic reference/normalization check; all allele representations retained.

segregation.statement: De novo per individualS1 row6; Trio testing described in row7.

causal_confidence.statement: De novo hemizygous Y774C; DD/mildID, hypotonia, macroglossia/cleft palate, hernias, brain hemorrhages, airway malacia/stenosis. Main article attributes aortic root dilation/beta blocker to patient7, but individual S1 and case report say normal echocardiogram: source conflict retained. Allvariants originally laboratoryVUS because ZFX was a candidate gene; authors putatively upgrade using study evidence and acknowledge ACMG novel-gene limitations. Functional evidence supports gene/variant mechanisms, not automatic clinical pathogenicity of every individual.

Maternally inherited hemizygous R786Q; severe DD/moderateID/nonverbal ASD, airway/feeding support, Pierre-Robin/cleft palate, cardiac anomalies and hyperparathyroidism. causal_confidence.statement: Maternally inherited hemizygous R786Q; severe DD/moderateID/nonverbal ASD, airway/feeding support, Pierre-Robin/cleft palate, cardiac anomalies and hyperparathyroidism. Patient and mother have parathyroid hyperplasia; not an adenoma in patient8. Maternal tumor described as fibroma in supplement versus sarcoma in main text: unresolved source discrepancy. patient_identity.statement: Exact individual Patient9; S1L3 identifies this case. De novo heterozygous R786Q in46,XX individual who is a man; gender identity does not establish hemizygosity. X-inactivation skewed. Normal averageIQ, autistic traits rather than formal ASD diagnosis inS1, hyperparathyroidism/adenoma, vascular anomalies and thyroid carcinoma. Separate inherited KCNH2 c526C>T R176W explains QT phenotype per authors; hypermobility/EDS clinical diagnosis also reported.

limitations: Source correspondence audit, not independent reproduction of molecular experiments or clinical validation.
All six main figures and complete main text read; case-relevant S1 mapped columns and all case reports read. S3–S6 omics workbooks remain unread.

Missense proteins retain broad DNA binding/transactivation; altered subsets show gain and loss, not complete inactivation. Assays delete partner factors ZNF711/ZFY and do not replicate patient cellular context.
ZebrafishKO has altered anxiety/habituation, normalgrossmorphology and nonsignificant social/mirror tests; not a validated humanIQ measure.
The primary source itself mixes genomic/transcript coordinates in Figure3, carries some contradictory case summaries, and initially classified all candidate-gene variantsVUS.
Packet phenotype exclusions often conflict with explicit source positives or encode absent documentation as a negative.
Public mainPDF and supplements preserved in externalpaper/reviewer-3.
